newsitem.title: UK: UK water stocks ease on price review news.
newsitem.headline: UK water stocks ease on price review news.

text.p: Shares in UK water stocks edged lower in early trading as regulatory wories resurfaced after industry watchdog Ofwat said it planned to review price limits for all 29 water and sewage firms in England and Wales in 1999. Thames Water slipped 4p to 548-1/2p, South West Water 1-1/2p to 672-1/2p and Severn Trent Water 4p to 600p but analysts played down the news saying it came as little surprise.
"It was virtually inevitable that there would be another price review before 2,000. I think that was seen as almost as certain as night following day," said Yamaichi's Nigel Hawkins.

Yorkshire Water, already the subject of a 1999 price review, eased 4-1/2p to 611-1/2p. "In the spirit of openness we are announcing the review now to remove speculation and regulatory uncertainty. I want to give sufficient time for consulattion with all those involved," said Ofwat director general Ian Byatt.

Recent droughts had shown a need for companies to give more attention to leakage control and maintaining a satisfactory balance between suppply and demand which would be a major consideration at the next review, said Byatt.

"This has been built into share prices and while it is true back in July 1994 Ofwat set out a pricing formula until the year 2005, those latter five years were on a very, very provisional basis," said Hawkins. make sure that when you come to negotiate leakage records have improved.'"
